case_question: Several of these libraries let a record be built either from nothing or out of an existing record, and the second path is where they go wrong. In one library, three producers of a derived record are each incomplete, and each is invisible until the record is derived rather than constructed. One of them, preparing a record just before it is stored, edits the sub-object it was handed instead of replacing it - harmless when that sub-object was made for the occasion, destructive when it belongs to the record being derived from, and an outright failure when that source is protected against writes. One of them, when a gradual transition between two versions of a record needs the shorter side padded out, mints the padding by copying an existing member and changing only what it thought of, so the padded members are indistinguishable to the step that later has to tell members apart, which keeps one and drops the rest. One of them rebuilds a composite in a new coordinate space out of its parts alone, so everything the composite had additionally been told about itself - how it should be treated, which of its parts to hold but disregard, what the caller asked to override - is absent from the result. A fourth producer, in a different library, reconstructs live state from a package that a different version of the same library may have written, and assumes every field the current version writes is present in it. The contract behind all four is that a derived record is a new and independent thing: it carries forward everything the original carried that the derivation does not deliberately replace, it is given its own identity wherever identity is what tells members apart, it tolerates an original written by an older or sparser producer, and it is never produced by writing into the original. Two further libraries in this folder make that discipline the centre of their core rather than an afterthought, and are the reference a complete derivation should be measured against. Which files derive a record incompletely, or by writing into its source, and which own the contract they have to be brought in line with?

retriever.surface: Opus 5 with ONLY the plumbline knowledge-graph MCP server: a remote Neo4j graph spanning the indexed repos. No Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, filesystem access to the checkouts, or subagents.
retriever.checkout_verified: run.sh gates on git rev-parse HEAD == pinned commit for all 15 repositories before launch
retriever.isolation: kernel-enforced by sandbox-exec with absolute subpaths: gold, the answer vault and every sibling arm are unreadable; no prior-run transcript is readable; fresh cwd; no settings sources loaded

cost.launch: fresh isolated `claude -p` under sandbox-exec, --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config with ONLY the plumbline MCP server (remote Neo4j knowledge graph, HTTP), --allowedTools the 20 mcp__plumbline__* tools and --disallowedTools Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Grep,Glob,WebFetch,WebSearch,Task,...
cost.cache_prefix_only_note: The first-turn cache read is the CLI's static system-prompt and tool-definition prefix, which is byte-identical across sessions on this machine and was warm from unrelated earlier sessions. It carries no case context: this run's own prompt shows up as cache_creation on that same turn, not as a read. So the RETRIEVAL measurement is clean; what is not comparable is the COST column.
cost.cost_comparability_note: This run had prompt caching ON (cache_read=1,874,501), so its CLI cost is a cached price. Sibling arms on other cases were run both ways, so cost columns are only comparable within a caching mode. Re-run with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 for a like-for-like cost number; the ranked answer does not change.
cost.cache_clean_note: cache_clean means no cache was inherited from an earlier session, which is what the run conditions require -- NOT that the run read no cache at all. In-run cache (the totals above) is expected and comparable. Judged on cache_read at the first assistant turn.
cost.surface_pure_note: Arm surface is Opus 5 with ONLY the plumbline knowledge-graph MCP server (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, shortest_path) against a single merged graph. Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Write/Edit and every other MCP server are excluded by --disallowedTools and --strict-mcp-config, so a filesystem-grep escape was not merely unused but impossible. Any tool outside the plumbline allow-list counts as a surface violation.

sandbox.mechanism: sandbox-exec (macOS seatbelt), profile pinned at sandbox.sb
sandbox.gate4_verified_both_ways: before launch, the profile was proved to deny golden.json AND the pinned repo checkouts, while still allowing mcp_plumbline.json. Checking only unreadability is what let an earlier stale path pass a profile that denied nothing.
sandbox.note: The benchmark tree is denied wholesale and the ONLY re-allowed path is the single file mcp_plumbline.json (the MCP config the CLI must read to start). The pinned checkouts themselves stay unreadable -- this arm reaches code solely through the remote graph -- and golden.json and every sibling arm's results fail with EPERM. ~/.claude/projects is denied too, so no earlier session transcript - nor this run's own - is readable. cwd was a fresh empty directory, no settings sources were loaded and slash commands were disabled, so no CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins or hooks applied; auto-memory is unreadable under the sandbox.

cost.prompt_caching: default (in-run caching allowed by this case's run conditions)

index.index_repo_gap_note: index_repo_gap lists roster repos with NO knowledge row at all: gold in them is unreachable on this surface. index_commit_drift lists repos whose newest indexed commit differs from the pinned one; the pinned commit may still be indexed (indexedCommitCount>1) but is not the default snapshot. Neither list explains a miss in a repo that appears in neither.
